topic: Introduction to Engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS) & Electronic centralized Aircraft Monitoring (ECAM)
syllabus_extract: Introduction to Engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS) & Electronic centralized Aircraft Monitoring (ECAM). Practical on EICAS & ECAM.
specific_objectives: 20.7.1.1 Trainee Will Be able to explain electronic displays of engine performance parameters.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Practical on EICAS & ECAM: Demonstrate engine parameter display selection, verify alert message hierarchy, and simulate normal/abnormal mode transitions under instructor supervision.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of the EICAS system?
How does ECAM differ from traditional analog engine instruments?
List three common engine performance parameters displayed electronically.

development.content:
EICAS System Architecture Overview
Engine Performance Parameter Displays
Alert Message Hierarchy and Priority
Display Modes: Normal and Backup
Crew Alerting System Integration

ECAM System Architecture Overview
Normal and Abnormal Display Modes
Engine Parameter Monitoring on ECAM
Alert Message Categories and Actions
Comparison between EICAS and ECAM

Practical Demonstration of EICAS Display
Practical Demonstration of ECAM Display
Simulation of Alert Message Scenarios
Verification of Crew Alerting Functions
Instructor Supervision and Feedback

summary_questions: Explain the difference in alert message priority between EICAS and ECAM systems.
Describe how engine performance parameters are presented in normal versus backup modes.
Identify the primary advantage of electronic centralized monitoring over analog systems.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note comparing the display units and alert message handling of EICAS and ECAM for the next lesson (LP 18).

pft_rows.syllabus: EICAS Display units, Display modes, Display select panels and alert messages.
